ambiguities: The interacted specification is not written out as an equation in the paper; the column content is inferred from the table row labels and the text describing the heterogeneity check.

The paper writes that βj/100 is the percentage point change in the D-index per one percentage point change in the explanatory variable (pp. 7-8), but its own magnitude statements (e.g. −0.309 read as 0.309 percentage points) treat βj itself as that quantity; the units field follows the magnitude statements.

evidence.how: The paper states that the dependent variable and all explanatory variables are measured as fractions and that the coefficient is to be read as the percentage point change in the D-index of residential segregation induced by a one percentage point change in the respective explanatory variable over the same period (pp. 7-8); its own magnitude statements (pp. 10-11) read the printed coefficient itself in those units.

value.normalisation: Dependent variable and all explanatory variables measured as fractions; the paper writes that “βj/100 can be interpreted as the percentage point change in the D-index ... induced by a one percentage point change in the respective explanatory variable over the same period” (pp. 7-8), while its own magnitude statements read βj itself as percentage points per percentage point. The low-income share is the omitted income category: the low, middle and high income shares sum to one and only the high and medium shares enter the model. The interaction term estimated in this column is not part of the printed equation.
